To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tbp2 is efficiently expressed and matured when its natural signal peptide is replaced by an E. coli lipobox signal peptide.

the signal peptide is the major determinant for the maturation of Tbp2 in E. coli and that a signal peptide from E. coli lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis can be used for an efficient production of lipidated Tbp1 and Tpb2 in E. coli.
we developed a heterologous E. coli expression system to obtain a high amount of lipidated Tbp1 and TBP2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of a surface protein of the pathogen Neisseria meningitis in Escherichie coli and with the optimization of its maturation.
the expression of a Neisseria meningitis protein, Tbp2.
the production and characterization of a new meningococcal vaccine candidate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipidation of Tbp2 precursor is not an intrinsic characteristic of the protein but is dependent on the nature of the signal peptide.
the use of the signal peptide of the E. coli lipobox protein DsbB in combination with an optimized growth protocol allows for the production of high amounts of lipidated Tbp 2 in E. coli.
the lipidated form of Tbp2 is a good candidate as a potential vaccine component against N. meningitides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a large-scale production of lipidated Tbp-2 from E. coli and have shown the feasibility of using this system to produce other lipidated proteins.
Tbp2 can be efficiently produced in E. coli, with a signal peptide derived from a lipoprotein, and that the protein can be purified to homogeneity.
Tbp2 can be produced in large amounts in E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lipidation of the cysteine residue at the N terminus of Tbp2 is essential for its biological activity, and that this lipidation can be performed efficiently in E. coli. The
lipidation of the cysteine residue of the mature Tbp2 is essential to ensure a high expression level of the mature protein in E. coli.
lipidation is a key factor to optimize the production of surface proteins in heterologous expression systems.
